html:
SMTO-UI-0040 — This saved connection's details are damaged

GUID: 6e2ac2d5-81e5-4e4d-a910-b01c5b34369c
Slug: ui-http-configuration-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • This parameter is meant to hold the details for connecting to a web service, but those details are incomplete or in an older layout. SMTO can't show the usual connection form, so you'll need to fix the saved details.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Value tab, select Reveal & edit value and check the web address and sign-in details. Fix anything missing or wrong, then select Save. Correcting the saved details lets SMTO show the normal connection form again.
  2. If the details are too broken to fix, start a new parameter: in the template list above the parameter list, choose HTTP Connection (or the HTTP template that matches how the service signs in), select New, and fill in the form. The template starts with all the parts a working connection needs.
  3. If you made a new parameter, use its name with @ in your messages and workflows, then remove the old one with Delete parameter. Anything still using the old name would keep picking up the damaged details.

What success looks like

  • Opening the parameter shows the connection form with no error message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Never send passwords, tokens or keys from the connection.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The parameter is marked as an http_connection profile, but GET /api/agent/http/connections/:key returned 422, so its connection-profile editor cannot load and only the raw value editor is available.

What this means

  • A saved parameter is identified as an HTTP entry but cannot produce a usable HTTP profile editor projection. This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A saved parameter is identified as an HTTP entry but cannot produce a usable HTTP profile editor projection.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect profile shape and supported authentication/TLS fields through the authorized editor.

How to fix it

  • parameter_editor.js selectParameter() presents ui_http_configuration_invalid when entry.http_profile.profile_type is http_connection but httpDetail() gets 422 from /api/agent/http/connections/:key. Reveal the raw value and correct it to a valid profile (compare with the "HTTP Connection" template: profile_type, profile_version, base_url, auth, TLS fields), or recreate it from that template; keep secret values out of logs.
  • Reveal and edit the saved parameter through its supported profile editor. Validate authentication and TLS fields while keeping secrets private.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported saved HTTP profile loads into its editor.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
